content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Does anyone know if it's possible to apply a ramp to an analog output selected by a multiplexer? I have four inputs (from an operator display), which determine the voltage sent to my inverter. I would like the ramp to be used only when one specific input is chosen (F4), not for the others. The issue is that the machine can't initially handle heavy material coming off it. My thoughts were to either use a pulse relay output for an initial period—where the stop time is much longer than run time (no ramp)—or apply a ramp initially to slow the motor to the lowest speed. Not sure which is more practical or easier to set up. Any advice would be appreciated. Sincerely,

Hello, By using a block ramp, you can configure the L1 and/or L2 parameters via a pointer to another block (like counters or analog blocks). This might address your question. Additionally, I'm sharing some example circuits that might inspire you to create your own ramp function, with control options as needed. Best regards, [user_name]
Dear [user_name], Thank you for your assistance. I'll review the code to understand it better—I'm still quite new to programming with this controller. Thanks again and have a great day. Sincerely,

There is uncertainty about feasibility and implementation method.
